cr_rationale: Minor single-casualty RTC on the approach to a live flats fire with people at risk. The priority is to clear and keep open the blue-light corridor, not to over-resource. I am sending 1 ambulance, which meets the floor, plus 2 patrol cars and 1 roads policing unit. The RRV is dropped because ambulance availability is high and the RRV is better held for Park Hill. Fire is deliberately not tasked: police take ownership of the lamp post hazard through the council contractor, which closes the UNROUTED_AGENCY_NEEDED flag without drawing appliances from a life-risk fire. Closure is partial only, and there is one shared RVP on Talbot St.

routing.rationale: Single-vehicle RTC into lamp post, Duke Street / Talbot Street. One casualty, dazed but conscious: ambulance to assess for head or neck injury. Police lead for scene safety and traffic control because of live traffic, and to manage the collision report. Fire not required: no persons trapped and no fuel leak, fire or other fire hazard reported. Keep fire capacity for INC-3AB47A3E, the pending severity 4 structure fire at Park Hill, South Street, 354 m away with people reported on a balcony. Treat as a separate incident, not a duplicate. Police should keep the route clear for fire appliances heading to INC-3AB47A3E. Re-route fire to this RTC if a lamp post collapse, fuel leak or entrapment is reported.

mission_details.summary: Single-vehicle RTC: a car hit a lamp post at the bottom of Duke Street / Talbot Street after swerving to avoid a fire engine. One casualty, conscious but dazed, not trapped. The scene sits on the main approach to an active flats fire at Park Hill 354 m away. Police lead: protect the scene, manage traffic and keep the blue-light corridor open, and investigate the collision.
tactical_plan: First patrol car places a fend-off position upstream, using a single lane only, and sets a 20 m inner cordon around the vehicle and lamp post.
Second patrol car manages traffic at the Talbot Street junction and keeps Duke Street flowing for fire appliances and ambulances heading to Park Hill.
Tell ambulance control the open route: Duke Street both directions, with Talbot Street as the secondary approach.
Roads policing unit carries out collision investigation: scene photography, vehicle positions, driver details, breath test once medically appropriate, and witness and dashcam canvass.
Identify the fire appliance involved, if possible, for witness and dashcam evidence via fire control, after the fire incident allows.
Arrange vehicle recovery quickly to clear the route; reopen the lane once recovery and lamp post safety are confirmed.
Escalate to full closure plus a forensic collision investigator only if injuries are reassessed as life-changing, and then route fire and ambulance via alternative approaches.
hazards_identified: Live traffic on Duke Street, including high-speed blue-light appliances heading to the nearby fire
Damaged lamp post: possible collapse and exposed electrical cabling
Vehicle fluid leaks and debris on the carriageway
Smoke drift from the Park Hill fire may reduce visibility
Casualty with possible head injury who may deteriorate
safety_notes: All officers in high-visibility clothing; vehicles fend off with emergency lights on.
Keep clear of the lamp post fall zone until it is confirmed safe.
Do not obstruct the Duke Street blue-light corridor; coordinate continuously with fire control on appliance movements.
Preservation of life takes precedence over evidence.

mission_details.summary: Minor-to-moderate RTC at Duke Street / Talbot Street with 1 conscious, dazed driver and no entrapment. Response is 1 emergency ambulance (P1) plus an RRV (P2). No critical care car is needed because the KB criteria are not met. Crews must not obstruct fire access to the concurrent Park Hill flats fire 354 m away.
tactical_plan: Dispatch the nearest emergency ambulance and the RRV on blue lights. Approach via Talbot Street and avoid the fire appliance routes to Park Hill.
Position vehicles in a fend-off configuration, protected by the police traffic cordon.
Carry out a primary survey, assess GCS and do neuro observations for the dazed presentation.
Assess the C-spine using mechanism and clinical criteria, and immobilise if indicated.
Convey to the Royal Hallamshire Hospital (ETA 4.4 min) if the patient is stable with no major trauma triggers.
Divert to Northern General (MTC, ETA 8 min) if major trauma triggers develop, such as a falling GCS or significant injury.
Upgrade to a critical care car if the deterioration meets the major trauma threshold.
Release the RRV after the ambulance arrives if it is not needed, so it is available for the Park Hill fire.
hazards_identified: Damaged lamp post: risk of collapse and exposed electrical cabling
Vehicle fluid leaks or airbag deployment
Concurrent structure fire nearby with heavy emergency vehicle movement and possible smoke drift
safety_notes: Hi-vis PPE is required. Work within the police-protected zone only.
Do not approach the lamp post if cabling is exposed until it is made safe.
Do not block fire service access to Park Hill.
Crews do not enter any area declared unsafe by police or fire.

directives.action: Fend off upstream on lower Duke St; cone the offside lane only and set a 20 m inner cordon round the car and lamp post.
Keep Duke St flowing both ways for fire appliances to Park Hill; no full closure.
Stage kerbside at the Talbot St RVP 40 m off the junction; enter via the police-marked approach path to the casualty.
Assess the driver for head and C-spine injury; convey to Royal Hallamshire, or Northern General if trauma triggers are met.
Hold a fall-zone exclusion round the lamp post and request the council street-lighting contractor now.
Roads policing: photograph the scene, take driver and witness details, breath test once cleared medically, then recover the vehicle fast.
Do not divert from Park Hill; tell police which appliance was on Duke St at 14:40 once the fire allows.

findings: An ambulance reached the injured driver in 2.2 minutes and two patrol cars arrived in 3.1 minutes, well inside both targets.
All essential units were sent with full crews and no unmet needs.
Duke Street was kept open both ways so fire engines could still reach the nearby Park Hill flats fire.
One requested unit was trimmed from the plan with no loss of essential cover, and the roads policing unit arrived later at 7.1 minutes for the collision investigation.
evaluation.headline: Driver hurt dodging fire engine on Duke Street as crews keep route to Park Hill fire open
evaluation.dek: An ambulance, two patrol cars and a roads policing unit were sent after a car hit a lamp post; police kept traffic moving so fire engines could reach a nearby flats fire.
